packet.title: Laziness, joins and the step limit (implementation)

body.p: After , , and (writing the book's performance chapter found three things): head(filter(1 to 1e9, ...)) and exists((1 to 1e9)[. = 999]) read the whole range; the chapter's join of 2,000 orders takes 12 s although 's filter index exists for it; the default step limit takes about 75 s to trigger.

item.p: Mechanism: one general mechanism for stopping early (head, exists, empty, [1], some/every, boolean()), on the one IR and evaluator, with , honest step counts and the errors XPath 4.0, 2.4.3 lets be skipped; the filter index extended in general to the join's shape; the step rate measured and the default limit decided without touching the drivers' budgets (, ).

Owns: src/evaluator.c, src/evaluator_index.c, src/ir_loop_passes.c, src/ir.c (the pass list, the text form), src/ir_internal.h and src/ir_pass_internal.h (their LET and pass parts), the traversal of src/function_library_higher_order.c, tests/bench/, tests/ir_loop_passes_test.c, docs/book/src/performance.md and its examples.

Done when: each change measured before and after, in a D-record and the commit messages; no QT4 XQ40 or XT40 outcome changes, case by case; the book's chapter true (). Done 2026-10-20 (): descendant paths, the number view and non-constant probes first (the book's join 12.9 to 0.045 s); item demands and quantified fusion (exists, head(filter(...)), [1], some/every over 10^7 items 2 to 6 s to 0.004 s); the default step bound 10^8 (8 s instead of 75 s; the drivers' bounds unchanged); xmark-all +1 % instructions; QT4 XQ40 and XT40 unchanged case by case.
